explanation: Iterate inorder with an explicit stack and stop at the kth value. BST inorder visits keys in sorted order.
timeComplexity: O(h + k) time for height h and rank k.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Inorder traversal visits strict BST keys in increasing order. The explicit stack simulates that traversal, so the kth removed node is exactly the kth smallest key. Stopping there cannot skip any smaller key and avoids visiting unnecessary later nodes.
walkthrough: For [10,4,16,2,7,13,19] and k=4, inorder begins 2,4,7,10. The fourth visited value is 10, so return 10.
edgeCases: k is 1-based and lies within the node count.
The explicit stack uses tree height rather than a copied tree.
